pr_body:
##### Summary
Report reason why ACLK build failed. Respect opt out.

Fixes #8050

##### Component Name

##### Test Plan
Simulate ACLK build failure (e.g. by removing libomosq.a from `externaldeps` folder and rerun configure without running installer).

You should see events in Google Analytics.

Keep in mind changes merged by Andrew meanwhile (you must pass --with-cloud to configure instead of ACLK=yes). If cloud is not enabled by purpose do not report anything.

##### Additional Information
pr_comments:
Manage this branch in Squash

Test this branch here: https://underhoodreport-aclk-install-f-mvxxs.squash.io
The parts of the configure that you are updating have changed recently, please rebase and rework around the new structure.

- Removed `cmake`
- Executed with `--cloud-testing`

Result at the end of compilation process
```
The following non-fatal errors were encountered during the installation process:

* Failed to build libwebsockets. The install process will continue, but you may not be able to connect this node to Netdata Cloud.
```

however the agent was build with ACLK enabled because I had libwebsockets.a available from previous run.

I am guessing the `may not be able`  in that message leaves some hope to work?

Hi, that message is from installer in master. Not related to this PR at all. We can ask @Ferroin if we want better handling in installer.

This PR is about Agent reporting to Google Analytics independent of installer.
It's fine - it requires the user to explicitly reach that state and the message reads "may".

I am seeing that a file is created `aclk_report_sent` so that the report is not send twice. 

I can't find anything in the specs that specifies that. Did I miss something?
Well as far as I understand the point is to know how many ACLK builds failed. Not how many times agent without ACLK is started.
rebased on master and skipped the commit that was adding the override as requesteb by @amoss

issue_context.title: During the agent installation, if the ACLK fails to be built, show an error message to the user
issue_context.body:
#### Summary

Ensure that the requirement in product#282 are met.

- [x] If ACLK error reporting not set yet by #8051 define it with this issue
- [x] If ACLK build fails make it prominent to the user so he knows about it. It should not be just small line easily overlooked in log. @amoss will speak to @jacekkolasa about this separately.
- [x] Netdata should log on startup it is build without ACLK
- [x] Report failure to Cloud to same endpoint #8051 
- [x] Respect DO_NOT_TRACK environment variable

(Some of this will be covered by PR 8025 but there are fresh requests at the bottom of the discussion).

review_comments:
I think we need to remove the file and send everytime (just as we do with START/ EXIT)

The file is never removed (as far as I can see) even if there is a successful build.

If we have a successful build followed by a failed one (say a month later) we want to know that.
Hmmm, well in such case we might want to get product involved as the task seems to be different.

No this does not seem to be correct. We want to know where installation failed because the dependency was unavailable. The case where it worked, but the user is recompiling it in the same source tree and it then fails does not seem to be relevant to the ask. What they care about is that if somebody tries to install it and the ACLK can't be enabled then we find out about it.
I understand the ask as being per-installation rather than per-compile.
then we have to delete it from installer
I don't think that it needs to be deleted at all - if the failure has been reported then there is no need to report it again from the same machine.
